title: How to Calculate Your Average BBL Salary: Hourly to Annual and Fortnightly Pay
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay using a 38-hour week. Understand tax, super, and the National Minimum Wage for your average bbl salary.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, an hourly rate of $26.44 gives a weekly pay of $1004.90 and an annual gross of $52,254.80 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the current National Minimum Wage in Australia?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 ordinary hours. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and apply to award/agreement-free employees.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for entitlements like paid leave. For example, if your base rate is $26.44, the casual rate becomes $33.05. When using [the timesheet](/), you can check a box to automatically add this loading. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my pay?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). It is not deducted from your pay. For example, on a weekly wage of $1004.90, your employer contributes $120.59 to your super fund. The super guarantee stops at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Average BBL Salary

When you're negotiating a job offer or comparing roles, knowing your **average bbl salary** helps you see the full picture. Whether you're paid by the hour or on a salary, converting between the two is straightforward once you know the formula. This guide uses the standard 38-hour week and the latest Fair Work and ATO figures to show you how your hourly rate translates into weekly, fortnightly, and annual pay, plus what you can expect after tax and super.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours, that's:

- **Weekly pay** = hourly rate × 38
- **Fortnightly pay** = weekly pay × 2
- **Annual pay** = weekly pay × 52

For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00, your weekly pay is $1,140.00, your fortnightly pay is $2,280.00, and your annual gross is $59,280.00. This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use [the timesheet](/) to enter your own rate and see these figures instantly.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the **National Minimum Wage** each year. From 1 July 2026, the rate is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, giving a weekly minimum of $1,004.90. This is the base for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most employees, however, are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. You can find the correct pay rates for your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) page.

### Casual Loading

If you're a casual employee, you're entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that's $33.05 per hour. The loading compensates for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. When using our calculator, tick the casual loading checkbox – never add it yourself. See [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) for more.

## Average Weekly Earnings Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) figures. In May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, while total earnings for all employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week. These figures give you a benchmark for your **average bbl salary** – but remember, your actual pay depends on your award, experience, and hours. For more comparisons, check our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

## Tax and Medicare Levy

Your gross annual pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies marginal tax rates for 2026–27:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

In addition, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The low-income thresholds for the Medicare levy reduction are based on 2025–26 figures (single threshold $24,276) as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage ($52,254.80 annually), the tax would be approximately $6,676 and Medicare $1,045, leaving a take-home of about $44,534. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

## Superannuation

Super is paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings, not deducted from your pay. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So on a weekly wage of $1,004.90, your employer contributes $120.59 to your super fund. This is separate from your take-home pay. Learn more on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For the National Minimum Wage, that's $2,009.80. After tax and Medicare, a fortnightly take-home might be around $1,712 (depending on your total annual income). This can help with budgeting and comparing job offers.

## Putting It All Together

To find your **average bbl salary**, start with your hourly rate. Multiply by 38 for weekly, then by 52 for annual. Add 25% if you're casual. Then subtract estimated tax and Medicare to see your take-home. Remember, this is an estimate – your actual pay may vary due to overtime, allowances, salary sacrifice, or HELP repayments. For a quick calculation, visit [the timesheet](/) and enter your details.

### Important Notes

- The formula assumes a consistent 38-hour week with no unpaid breaks.
- Award rates may be higher than the National Minimum Wage – always check your award.
- Super is paid on top and does not reduce your take-home.
- Tax estimates use the 2026–27 resident rates and full tax-free threshold.
- This is not financial advice; consult a professional for your specific situation.
